prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1066; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the policyholder reported being struck while turning left at an intersection. The claimant was a passenger in the other vehicle and has retained counsel, so all contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Both drivers gave statements that match the reported sequence of events.

Entry 3: Spoke with two independent witnesses who saw the left-turn collision and confirmed it happened as described. Photos from the scene show damage consistent with the reported impact.

Entry 4: Inspected the vehicle and found the damage lines up with the described impact point and force. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 5: Confirmed the driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member under the policy. Coverage questions are resolved for the driver.

Entry 6: The claimant reported a knee injury and provided medical records. The injury fits the type and force of a side-impact collision, and no prior injury to the same body area is on record.

Entry 7: Claimant's account has stayed the same in every conversation, including the initial call, the recorded statement, and the follow-up through counsel.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits that tapered as the claimant's knee improved. Billing records match the documented care.

Entry 9: Based on the evidence gathered so far, the claim is supported across the accident, the vehicle damage, the injury, and coverage. File remains open pending final medical bills and attorney demand.
